name: Lying Single-Leg Cable Knee Curl
description: The lying single-leg cable knee curl attaches a cuff to the ankle and uses the low cable pulley to provide constant tension throughout the curl, unlike the lying leg curl machine which has variable resistance. Training one leg at a time addresses imbalances. The cable provides resistance from a consistent angle, training the hamstrings in a slightly different tension curve than a machine.

execution.starting_position: Attach an ankle cuff to the low cable pulley. Lie prone on a flat bench placed in front of the cable stack. Attach the cuff to one ankle, leg extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Position the bench a few feet in front of the cable machine so the cable pulls the ankle directly away from the machine at floor level.
steps: Step 1: Lie face-down on the bench, ankle cuff attached.
Step 2: Curl the working leg upward by bending the knee, pulling the cable against resistance.
Step 3: Curl until maximum knee flexion is reached.
Step 4: Lower the leg slowly back to the starting position, maintaining cable tension throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Hips rising off the bench to generate momentum
safety_considerations: Ensure the ankle cuff is securely fastened before beginning
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension to maximum knee flexion. The cable maintains tension throughout — do not rush.
coaching_cues: Lead with the heel toward the glute
Feel the stretch at the bottom
